claim_card.quantifiers: For every n : Nat and f : Fin n -> Real -> Complex, with every f_i continuous and of bounded variation on Icc 0 1 and f_i(1)=f_i(0).
claim_card.conclusion: (cycleOfRectifiable n f hv hc hclosed).length <= sum_i geometricLength(f_i).
claim_card.coefficient_domain: Real nonnegative lengths; velocities in Complex; Lebesgue interval integrals.
claim_card.exceptional_cases: No lower bound on n or length; no injectivity, smoothness, original absolute continuity, nonvanishing speed, or extension regularity required. Domain is the normalized unit interval.
claim_card.recorded_status: Candidate source header says not yet compiled; this audit independently compiled the final SHA256 successfully. The stale header has no mathematical effect.

definitions.name: coordinateVelocity
definitions.meaning: ofReal(deriv(Re o f)(x)) + ofReal(deriv(Im o f)(x))*I. Each real derivative is zero when that coordinate is not differentiable. It equals the genuine real-variable complex derivative when both coordinates are differentiable. It need not equal deriv f at other points.

definitions.name: geometricLength
definitions.meaning: (eVariationOn f (Icc 0 1)).toReal. eVariationOn is the supremum of sums of Euclidean complex distances along ordered finite partitions. hv ensures finiteness, so toReal is the genuine finite variation rather than the infinity-to-zero convention.

definitions.name: unitIntervalPath
definitions.meaning: g(s)=naturalParameterization f (Icc 0 1) 0 (geometricLength(f)*s). naturalParameterization is f composed with Function.invFunOn of the cumulative variation map, with default point 0. Only its values on [0,1] and its interior derivatives are controlled/needed.

definitions.name: IntegralCycle.length
definitions.meaning: sum over Fin Gamma.count of the Lebesgue interval integral from 0 to 1 of norm(Gamma.velocity_i). For cycleOfRectifiable, velocity_i is exactly coordinateVelocity(unitIntervalPath f_i). It counts every Fin-index occurrence, without cancelling repeated or oppositely oriented loops.

obligations.name: Normalized continuous BV closed paths
obligations.evidence: Exactly hv, hc, hclosed; no hidden geometric restrictions in cycleOfRectifiable.

obligations.name: n=0
obligations.evidence: Both sums are empty and zero; pointwise proofs quantify over empty Fin 0.

obligations.name: Constant and zero-length paths
obligations.evidence: K=geometricLength=0 is permitted NNReal; unitIntervalPath(s)=arcPath(f)(0), constant for all s; no division by length occurs.

obligations.name: Repeated family entries, multiple traversals, backtracking, self intersections
obligations.evidence: Fin-index sums count repeats; variation counts ordered traveled distance. No quotient by trace or injective-path assumption.

obligations.name: Original singular continuous BV parametrizations
obligations.evidence: Only reconstructed unitIntervalPath is differentiated and required Lipschitz. No derivative theorem is asserted for the original f.

obligations.name: One or both coordinate nondifferentiability at an interior point
obligations.evidence: All Boolean cases handled by actual deriv default convention, avoiding an unjustified all-points Rademacher claim.

obligations.name: Endpoints and arbitrary outside extensions
obligations.evidence: Pointwise bound only on Ioo a b. Lebesgue integral comparison removes endpoint singletons; global derivative of the extension is never assumed bounded there.

obligations.name: Degenerate interval a=b in intermediate integral bound
obligations.evidence: hab allows equality; both interval integral and (b-a)K are zero; Ioo is empty.

obligations.name: Exact equality between velocity length and geometric variation
obligations.evidence: Only <= is proved. Equality is neither a hypothesis nor needed for the stated length bridge.

obligations.name: Contour equality for original oriented Riemann-Stieltjes integrals
obligations.evidence: No contour invariance theorem appears here; trace equality alone would not suffice.

decisive_scope_examples: For f(t)=t+i|t| at t=0, coordinateVelocity f 0=1, although f is not real-differentiable there and deriv f 0 defaults to 0. This does not contradict the proved bound; it explains why the coordinate case split is necessary.
An original singular continuous BV loop is allowed even when its original coordinate derivative misses geometric variation; the candidate differentiates its arclength reconstruction instead.
Repeated occurrences contribute repeated summands on both sides even though the trace union ignores multiplicity.
